scope: Sums of two and three complete rank-one 2x2 Schur packets G_i=w_i v_i v_i^T, with a separate Hermitian comparison

conventions.nondegenerateWeights: all displayed classification theorems assume w_i != 0; zero weights reduce to a lower-packet stratum

twoPacketClassification.conclusion: Neither complex phases nor opposite-sign weights create a nonaligned two-packet cancellation branch. The only nondegenerate zero is the common projective ray.

threePacketClassification.identity: det(sum_i G_i)=w_1 w_2 Delta_12^2+w_1 w_3 Delta_13^2+w_2 w_3 Delta_23^2
threePacketClassification.minorCoordinates: For a 2x3 coupling matrix the three minors have no Plucker relation; every nonzero projective minor triple is realized on a coordinate chart.
threePacketClassification.nonalignedCancellationStratum: The nonzero points of the weighted quadratic cone q_w(Delta)=0
threePacketClassification.geometryOverComplexNumbers: For nonzero weights q_w is nondegenerate. Its projectivization is a smooth irreducible conic in P^2_C, while the affine cone is singular only at the common-ray vertex Delta=0.

geometryOverRealNumbers.sameSignWeights: q_w is definite, so there is no nonaligned real zero.
geometryOverRealNumbers.mixedSignWeights: q_w has signature (1,2) or (2,1), so its nonzero real null cone supplies nonaligned cancellations.

threePacketClassification.rankOnNonalignedCone: The resulting 2x2 sum has rank exactly one. It cannot vanish because a nondegenerate three-dimensional symmetric form has Witt index one, whereas vanishing would require two independent mutually orthogonal null rows.
threePacketClassification.interpretation: Three is the minimal packet number for a phase or indefinite-sign cancellation that is not projective alignment.

perturbativeStratification.commonRayVertex: In packet-minor coordinates q_w has zero gradient at Delta=0. A small misalignment Delta=epsilon h lifts the determinant at order epsilon^2.
perturbativeStratification.nonalignedCone: At every nonzero null point grad(q_w) is nonzero. A generic transverse packet perturbation lifts the determinant at order epsilon.
perturbativeStratification.matrixSpaceBoundary: The quadratic protection at the common-ray vertex applies only to complete-packet deformations. An independent primitive 2x2 matrix deformation can lift a rank-one sum linearly.
perturbativeStratification.naturalnessVerdict: The nonaligned cone is an extended algebraic locus rather than an isolated numerical accident, but kinematics does not force a theory onto it. Technical protection requires an additional constraint that preserves and enforces null minor data.

coneStabilizers: O(3,C) after complex square-root rescaling of nonzero weights
O(1,2) or O(2,1) for real mixed-sign weights
symmetryBoundary.whatStabilizerDoes: It preserves the quadratic cone and can move between its nonzero points.
symmetryBoundary.whatStabilizerDoesNotDo: Invariance of q_w does not by itself impose q_w=0 on the coupling matrix.
symmetryBoundary.openPhysicalTest: Determine whether the actual Pati-Salam/Spin(2,3) carrier supplies a representation, orbit condition, or composite matching law that forces the minor vector to be null.

hermitianComparison.identity: For H=sum_i w_i v_i v_i^dagger with real weights, det(H)=sum_{i<j} w_i w_j |Delta_ij|^2.
hermitianComparison.positiveWeights: Only the common-ray stratum survives, for any complex phases.
hermitianComparison.mixedSignWeights: A real signed null cone remains possible from three packets onward.

spin23Signpost: The three minors form a natural quadratic three-vector. Its mixed-sign cancellation locus is an SO(1,2) null cone, giving a precise possible Spin(1,2)-inside-Spin(2,3) middle to test, not a derivation of that middle.
verdict: Claim 1509 is exact for two packets and for positive Hermitian sums. For three complex-symmetric or real-indefinite packets there is a distinct nonaligned null-cone branch; it is linearly fragile to generic packet perturbations and remains physically unprotected until the carrier forces null minor data.
